newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SWEET CRUDES RECOVER AGAINST FIRMER OUTRIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SWEET CRUDES RECOVER AGAINST FIRMER OUTRIGHTS.

text.p: Sweet crude grades in the U.S. Gulf popped slightly higher Tuesday morning on support from stronger Dated Brent values in the North Sea.

Outright benchmark crude September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood 20-25 cents higher at $19.85-95 a barrel, with the spread between September and October WTI around minus 13-15 cents, down from more than 20 cents late Monday.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold at 17-18 cents over the benchmark, some four to five cents stronger than Monday.
"It looks like the Dated Brent getting a little stronger did the job for LLS," said a cash trader in the Gulf.

Other deals saw West Texas Sour/Midland sell at firmer values, with the grade moving at $1.44-$1.50 under WTI. Postings Plus also sold at $1.90 and $1.91, and Midland/WTI at at steady WTI -33 cents, traders said.
